scenes.title: 1975 Oban Scottish Loch Shore & Pier: Scuba Divers With Waterproof Formica Slates Comparing the 2×2 'Dry-Dry (13.5) vs Wet-Wet (11.4)' Crossover
scenes.era: 1975, Loch pier & pebble shore, Oban, Scotland

layout.description: Crisp high-key sunlit Scottish loch-side diving pier and clear shallow turquoise-glass observation tank/dock: on the dry wooden pier sits Diver Group A in black-and-white wetsuits writing on clipboards (**Dry -> Dry: 13.5**), while visible down beside the clear sunlit pier ladder hovers Diver Group B in vintage 1975 twin-hose scuba masks writing with graphite pencils on **weighted white Formica underwater slates** (**Wet -> Wet: 11.4 vs Mismatched 8.5!**).

positions.who: Alan Baddeley & Duncan Godden (mannequins in 1975 Scottish wool cable-knit sweaters and windbreakers)
positions.where: standing on the sunlit wooden pier holding the underwater audio intercom cable and pointing to the 2×2 Crossover Scorecard ('Same Context Wins: 13.5 & 11.4 vs Mismatched: 8.6 & 8.4')

positions.who: Scuba Diver mannequins (in 1975 wetsuits, masks tilted on forehead on pier / writing on white Formica slate in clear sunlit water)
positions.where: comparing their waterproof Formica word slates across matched vs mismatched runs
positions.facing: at pier steps and clear water edge

props.name: weighted white Formica underwater writing slates & graphite pencils
props.period_detail: authentic 1975 waterproof recording method used at 20-foot depth
props.physical_behavior: makes underwater memory testing tangible and memorable

props.name: 2×2 Context Crossover Board ('DRY-DRY 13.5 | DRY-WET 8.6 | WET-DRY 8.4 | WET-WET 11.4')
props.period_detail: proves the diagonal X-shaped interaction at a single glance

actions.verb_sequence: reads 36 words over the diver headphone line -> Diver underwater writes smoothly on the white Formica slate (11.4 words matched vs 8.4 when brought ashore!)
traces the X-shaped crossover showing matched environments boosting free recall ~46%

reactions.reaction: grin comparing how jumping BACK into the cold water unlocked words they couldn't recall dry on the beach!

scenes.wardrobe: 1975 Scottish coastal fieldwork: chunky cream cable-knit wool fisherman sweaters, weatherproof windbreakers, vintage neoprene diving suits.
scenes.lighting: Crisp bright Highland coastal daylight over clear sunlit water and pale wood.
scenes.recognition_hook: Memorize 36 words twenty feet underwater: dry on the beach you blank out at 8.4 words — jump back into the cold loch and 11.4 words come rushing back!

key_visual.description: a sunlit 1975 Scottish wooden diving pier where researchers in cable-knit sweaters hold a 2x2 Dry/Wet crossover chart beside scuba divers comparing white waterproof Formica writing slates

scenes.title: 1980 Follow-Up Surprise: Multiple-Choice Recognition Wipes Out the Gap!

layout.description: Same sunlit pier dock where divers circle multiple-choice word sheets instead of blank slates.

positions.where: comparing identical high scores across all four Dry/Wet boxes on multiple-choice recognition

props.name: Multiple-Choice Slate ('Context Gap = 0%!')
props.period_detail: reassures students taking multiple-choice exams in unfamiliar halls

actions.verb_sequence: checks recognized words rapidly on dry land after underwater study with zero loss

reactions.reaction: notes context cues drive *search*, not recognition

scenes.recognition_hook: Hand those exact same divers a multiple-choice test instead of a blank slate, and the underwater-vs-land gap vanishes completely!

scenes.title: Walking Back to the Bedroom Doorway ('Why Did I Come Into the Kitchen?')

layout.description: Bright doorway between a study desk and a kitchen counter.

positions.where: standing puzzled in the kitchen ('Wait, what did I come for?'), then taking three steps back to see the study desk — snapping fingers as the answer pops back!

props.name: open doorway & study desk cue
props.period_detail: everyday context-reinstatement experienced by every human

actions.verb_sequence: pauses blankly in kitchen -> steps back to study threshold -> immediately remembers 'Scissors!'

scenes.recognition_hook: When you forget why you walked into the kitchen, retracing three steps back to the doorway works for the exact same reason Oban's divers jumped back in the loch!

scenes.title: 30-Second Mental Room Visualization in an Unfamiliar Exam Hall

layout.description: Sunlit rows of unfamiliar exam desks where a student pauses calmly before an essay prompt.

positions.where: closing eyes briefly for 20 seconds to picture their study desk lamp and notebook layout, then opening eyes and writing fluently

props.name: essay booklet & calm 20-second mental reset
props.period_detail: Steven Smith's (1979) Mental Context Reinstatement cure

actions.verb_sequence: closes eyes briefly reconstructing study context -> opens eyes and writes outline briskly

scenes.recognition_hook: Can't bring 20 feet of Scottish water into the exam hall? Close your eyes for twenty seconds and reconstruct your study desk inside your head!
